population.note: FICTIONAL. Arithmetic: ever-used 44.0 − on 34.8 = 9.2% of adults have used and are off now. There are 7.0 pts of new ever-users since 2032. Of them, 5.4 are on and 1.6 have already stopped (23%, close to the parent's 24%). Within the 37.0 pts who had used by 2032, 62% of the 27.9 then on stayed on (17.3; the parent rate was 60%, and conditional coverage plus cheap gray product nudged it up). The 10.6 who stopped joined the 9.1 already off, making a pool of 19.7. Of that pool, 12.1 restarted (61% over two years, against 57% in the parent; the increase is the $25–90 gray pen). So 17.3 + 12.1 = 29.4 on and 19.7 − 12.1 = 7.6 off. Totals: on 29.4 + 5.4 = 34.8; off 7.6 + 1.6 = 9.2. Cycled: 13.4 pts had cycled by 2032, plus ~5.5 first-time restarters in the old cohort and ~0.4 among new starters, gives 19.3 of 44.0 = 44%. Current users ≈ 94.0M of ~270M adults. Age bands weighted 20/33/24/23%: 4.0 + 12.87 + 12.41 + 5.52 = 34.8. Income thirds: (37 + 36 + 31.4)/3 = 34.8. The bottom third rose most (21.7 → 31.4), mostly on gray and HRSA product. The top third grew slowly (34 → 37) as thinness lost status there and some affluent users quit or moved to the muscle combination. 65+ rose 17 → 24 (~14.9M) on the dementia label, bone cover and the 2034 combination. Off-drug: ~24.8M adults have used and stopped. Many were cut off by conditions: Bridge 6-month non-responders, lockouts in ten Medicaid waiver states, and failed employer coaching or BMI gates. A growing minority are deliberate quitters who cite the 'unmedicated' ideal. ~151M adults have never used: organised refusers, the uninsured in non-expansion states, people with contraindications, and a new group of young adults who see the drug as their parents' thing. Pediatric: 1.1% of ~73M ≈ 800k, down from 880k. The 6–11 group fell from ~150k to ~70k after the Mar 2034 specialist-only restriction, while adolescent use held. About one child in three now lives with at least one parent on drug.

access.public_coverage: Medicare GLP-1 Bridge renewed in Dec 2033 through 2035. Payment falls from $225 to $195/month under SSA II, and the copay stays $50. Continuation conditions are retained (≥5% loss by month 6, ≥80% PDC, annual DEXA for 65+) and a chair-stand or grip-strength test is added at annual review. The bimagrumab+tirzepatide combination is covered only for 65+ who meet sarcopenia criteria, under prior authorisation. Bridge obesity users ≈4.6M × $195 × 12 ≈ $10.8B/yr. Medicare overall pays ≈15.4% of fills ≈14.5M users: ~13.9M of the 14.9M users aged 65+ (the other ~1.0M are cash or gray) plus ~0.6M disabled under-65. Medicaid pays ≈11.2% ≈10.5M users × $195 × 12 ≈ $24.6B/yr, federal and state combined. Ten states now run Indiana-style adherence waivers: Indiana, Arkansas, Missouri, Oklahoma, Georgia, Ohio and Montana, plus Kentucky, Louisiana and Arizona. HRSA Community Incretin Access Program: FY2034 appropriation $4.4B, with an annual verified weigh-in added as the price of renewal. It is no longer fully unconditioned. It serves ≈3.8M: 2.6M generic liraglutide × $60 × 12 = $1.87B, plus 1.2M semaglutide for cessation/AUD × $149 × 12 = $2.15B, total ≈ $4.0B, with the remainder spent on administration and weigh-in sites. TRICARE, VA and DoD cover ≈2.6M. That includes ~190k active-duty members in the Metabolic Readiness Program: 190k × $139 × 12 ≈ $317M/yr.
access.generic_rest_of_world: India has 100+ semaglutide and ~30 tirzepatide brands at $6–35/month. Mexico's border pharmacies sell generic semaglutide at ~$35–45. Canada, China, Brazil, Turkey and most of Asia and Latin America have legal generics. Chinese triple agonists are exported to Southeast Asia and the Gulf. US generic semaglutide launches scheduled for 2033 under patent settlements have been held by a Federal Circuit injunction on Novo's pen-injector device patent (Nov 2033), pending a 2035 trial. Tirzepatide remains protected to the mid-2030s.
access.note: FICTIONAL. Payer mix of ~94.0M users: commercial 36.2% (34.0M), Medicare 15.4% (14.5M), Medicaid 11.2% (10.5M), HRSA 4.0% (3.8M), TRICARE/VA/DoD 2.8% (2.6M), cash/direct 13.8% (13.0M), gray 16.6% (15.6M) = 100% and 94.0M. Managed decline: SSA II (Nov 2033) stepped TrumpRx/direct prices to $199 (semaglutide injection), $249 (tirzepatide), $149 (oral starts, unchanged) and $349 (retatrutide). Amycretin launched at $299 direct. Lilly's bimagrumab+tirzepatide combination (Stratara, May 2034) lists at $1,950 with a $599 direct price and is on allocation, the only brand above $300 that anyone pays. Wegovy list stays $1,349 and retatrutide list $1,499. Employer coverage reached 66%, and ~62% of covering employers attach conditions (PDC, 6-month loss, coaching). The gray market grew from ~9M to ~15.6M users (+73%). Drivers: the US generic delay against a $6–45 world price, ~25M people cut off by conditions, Mexican border-pharmacy purchases, Indian product trans-shipped through the UAE and Singapore to evade CBP mail seizures, and counterfeit pens sold through social-commerce storefronts. Gray pens cost $25–90/month. Skip-but-fill persists in conditioned plans. Some cut-off users now pair a gray pen with a separately filled covered antiresorptive.

'brain health' semaglutide for 50–64-year-olds outside the dementia label

drugs.pipeline_note: FICTIONAL. The muscle-preserving-combination driver is realised through the BLA filed in Mar 2032: FDA approved bimagrumab + tirzepatide (Stratara) in May 2034, 26 months after filing. Its phase 3 showed ~22% weight loss with lean-mass loss cut from ~35% to ~10% of total lost, measured by DXA. There is no falls or fracture endpoint, and the postmarketing requirement is a 5-year fracture study in 65+. Lilly sells it as 'Lose the fat. Keep the you.' Supply is limited (~0.4M users by year-end). Amycretin, under review at the start of the window, was approved Jul 2033. The mood/motivation driver is realised as new indications for an existing product: low-dose orforglipron for gambling disorder plus a labelled food-noise PRO claim (Mar 2033). No new molecular entity has a mood or depression indication. The incretin market is ≈$182B globally in 2034: US volume +26%, US net price −10 to −15%. Lilly and Novo cite the US generic injunction as 'temporary' in filings.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Still the leading cause of discontinuation. Rates are highest on retatrutide 12 mg and among gray users who skip titration or receive mislabelled strengths.

safety_ledger.effect: Gastroparesis, ileus and intestinal obstruction (mass tort)
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Persistence after stopping is still disputed. MDL 3094 has ~78,000 filed and tolled claims. Novo reached a partial settlement on the ileus track in 2034, and the gastroparesis track has no global deal.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Ileus labelled; FDA still declines to label persistent gastroparesis.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Absolute cases rise with volume and with retatrutide 12 mg.
Low absolute risk; no causal confirmation. The counterfeit and overdose clusters add confounded cases to the record.

NHANES-DXA 2031–33 confirms appendicular lean mass ~0.5 SD below matched non-users in 65+ users on drug for more than 2 years. Sarcopenia criteria are met at ~1.6–1.7× the rate, worst among gray and liraglutide users without protein or resistance-training support. Stratara reduces the DXA lean-loss share but has no functional or falls data yet.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Class Warning retained. Bridge adds a chair-stand or grip test at annual review. Stratara is approved with a 5-year fracture postmarketing requirement. HRSA sites still have no muscle requirement.

safety_ledger.effect: Bone mineral density loss and fragility fracture
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Medicare hip-fracture admissions rose a further ~3% in 2032–33. Modelled excess ≈ 13.9M Medicare users 65+ × ~0.5%/yr baseline × HR excess ~0.30 (lowered from 0.35 by bone cover) ≈ 21,000 hip fractures a year, concentrated in women, cyclers and people cut off by conditions. The final adolescent registry (Feb 2034) found lumbar BMD z-score accrual 0.17 SD lower after more than 3 years on drug, of which ~0.11 SD persists after adjusting for weight loss.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Baseline DEXA in Warnings for 65+ and postmenopausal women. Mar 2034 pediatric labelling: initiation in 6–11 restricted to pediatric specialists with baseline DEXA; adolescents get monitoring language. Endocrine societies keep antiresorptive co-prescription.

safety_ledger.effect: Denosumab-discontinuation rebound vertebral fractures in users who lose coverage
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: New in this window. Users dropped from the Bridge or Medicaid lose both drugs at once when their incretin and denosumab 'bone cover' sit on the same conditioned authorisation. Case series show multiple vertebral fractures within 12 months, a known denosumab effect now surfacing at population scale.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: AACE advisory to transition to zoledronate before any coverage end. CMS is reviewing whether to decouple antiresorptive authorisation from incretin continuation. No rule yet.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Conflicting cohorts; very low absolute risk.
No causal association, including in BED, AUD and gambling-disorder trials.

FDA's pooled class analysis (2033; 41 trials, ~62,000 participants) found a clinically meaningful SHAPS shift in 3.1% vs 1.9% at standard maintenance doses, and 7–8% on retatrutide ≥8 mg. Self-reported reduced pleasure among long-term users fell to ~8–11% as maintenance doses came down. About 31% report a deliberate dose holiday in the past year, down from ~45%.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Class labelling (Mar 2033) moved anhedonia to 'uncommon' adverse reactions, with the dose-dependent precaution kept for retatrutide. The same pharmacology underlies the gambling-disorder and food-noise claims. Broadcast and social DTC for behavioural claims has been barred since Mar 2034.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Driven by condition cut-offs, and now also by gray supply interruptions after CBP seizures and the counterfeit scares.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Indiana waiver litigation unresolved; no federal rule.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Protein, iron, B12 and vitamin D insufficiency signals persist, strongest among gray users with no clinical contact.

safety_ledger.effect: Long-horizon, adolescent, pediatric and cycling effects
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: About twelve years of adult and eleven years of adolescent follow-up. The bone-accrual question is partly answered (see bone entry). Pubertal-timing data were first reported in 2034 and are inconclusive. ~70k children aged 6–11 are on drug.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Pediatric registry continues; Mar 2034 specialist restriction for 6–11.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: This is now a public-health story. Poison-centre incretin calls are up ~60% on 2032. CDC's 2033–34 investigations found three main clusters: counterfeit 'Ozempic' pens containing insulin glargine (~1,100 ED visits for hypoglycaemia, 23 deaths), Burkholderia cepacia in reconstituted gray vials (~180 infections, 9 deaths), and mislabelled tirzepatide concentrations causing severe GI and dehydration admissions. Total ≈ 32 deaths confirmed over 14 months.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: CDC Health Alert (Aug 2033). FDA lot-verification app and pharmacy scan-check. CBP seizures doubled. Nine federal indictments of distributors and two of social-commerce storefront operators; users are not prosecuted. Personal land-border import is tolerated in practice.

safety_ledger.prevalence_note: A few percent, higher at 12 mg.
'Brain health' prescribing in 50–64-year-olds outside the label keeps growing. Those users carry the bone risk without proven cognitive benefit.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Label limits stated; no enforcement against off-label use.

safety_ledger.effect: Bimagrumab-specific effects (muscle spasm, diarrhoea, acne; long-term unknown)
safety_ledger.prevalence_note: Muscle spasms in ~20% early on and acne in a few percent in phase 3. Postmarketing exposure is small (~0.4M), plus an unmeasured gray-vial user base.
safety_ledger.regulatory_response: Labelled; 5-year fracture and cardiac postmarketing requirements.

food_and_beverage.state: Packaged-food volume keeps falling ~2.5–3% a year as a third of adults are on drug. The aesthetic inversion splits demand. Mass snacks and diet-branded products both fall, the second because 'diet' now reads as pen culture. A premium 'whole appetite' segment grows from a small base: full-fat dairy, butcher-counter meat, bakery. Protein and bone formats are now commodity products.

alcohol.state: US spirits and beer volume falls for a sixth year. The gambling-disorder and food-noise label claims extend reduced craving to more drinkers. Premium wine at dinner regains some status as a 'whole table' signal, but volume stays down.

restaurants.state: Value chains keep closing units in mid-income suburbs. Fine dining and steakhouses in Chicago, Austin and Nashville report the first cover growth in years, as finishing a tasting menu becomes a display of being unmedicated. The 'half plate' persists in fast casual.

apparel.state: Size runs stay wide. Fitted, shoulder-cut tailoring for built bodies sells at a premium, while 'pen-thin' straight cuts are discounted. Fall-safe senior apparel is mainstream.

fitness.state: Prescribed resistance training grows through Bridge tests and employer conditions. The aesthetic inversion adds 'earned muscle' boutique gyms, some advertising 'unmedicated floor' hours. Stratara's launch is marketed against them as muscle without the hours.

insurance.state: Pharmacy trend ~+7%. Plans ration through conditions. In Feb 2034 the Ninth Circuit held that adherence-feed premium differentials fail the 'reasonable alternative standard' where fill data do not show use. The Eighth Circuit upheld them in 2033. The resulting circuit split leaves differentials legal in some states and not others.

pharma.state: Lilly's national-champion bargain is extended through SSA II. Novo's margin compresses further and leans on amycretin and on the device patent holding off US generics. Indian generic makers dominate world volume and, indirectly, the US gray market. MDL reserves keep rising.

body_and_culture.what_the_body_signals: A thin body has become cheap and no longer signals much. It reads as medicated by default, at worst as $38 from across the border. The scarce signals are appetite, visibly eating a full meal and wanting it, and muscle that looks trained rather than injected. The new prestige phrase is 'unmedicated vitality'. Older bodies still carry a payer's conditions: DEXA, chair-stand, bone cover.
body_and_culture.thinness_and_class: The 'Charlotte build' has inverted. In Brooklyn and Silver Lake, college-educated women aged 25–39 now treat pen-thin as down-market and verify 'clean' status with $89 consumer peptide panels shared in dating profiles. Lower-income users are thinner than ever on gray product. Among the affluent old, Stratara and a trainer are the marker. Among the less affluent old, it is a bone-drug refill and a referral slip.
body_and_culture.eating_as_ritual: Open Table suppers have spread from church networks to secular 'whole table' dinner clubs in Austin and Denver. A plate eaten in public is a statement. Streamers do 'full plate' meals as a counter-genre. Families with one medicated parent describe dinners where the children and the unmedicated parent eat and the other parent watches.
body_and_culture.dating_and_intimacy: 'Unmedicated' is a premium filter on two dating apps, and 'on Stratara' is a selling point among over-55s. The negotiation over adherence windows has eased as holidays fell, but couples where one partner is gray-supplied argue about the counterfeit risk.
body_and_culture.meaning_of_appetite: Appetite has become a status good as well as a moral claim. 'Hunger is how we were made' is still a sermon line, and 'I eat' is now a fashion-magazine line. Five states (Tennessee, Idaho, Utah, South Dakota, West Virginia) bar employers from conditioning premiums on incretin use.

interior_life.reward_blunting_prevalence_note: FICTIONAL. FDA's 2033 pooled analysis put clinically meaningful anhedonia at 3.1% vs 1.9% at standard maintenance doses and 7–8% on retatrutide ≥8 mg. The label now lists it as uncommon. Self-reported reduced pleasure among long-term users is ~8–11%. Dose holidays fell from ~45% to ~31% of long-term users as maintenance doses came down and as users moved to MariTide or amycretin, which report fewer complaints. Low-dose Foundayo for BED, gambling disorder and food noise reached ~2.6M users by early 2034 inside the commercial and cash shares, then plateaued after the Mar 2034 ad bar.
interior_life.framing: In clinics it is an uncommon side effect: 'if you feel flat, we step down.' In Lilly's pre-ban marketing it was a treatment ('quiet mind', 'turn down the cravings'). 'The grey' survives as slightly dated slang, used ironically by people under 30. The backlash still says 'chemical contentment', but louder grievances have overtaken it.
interior_life.effect_on_work: Workplaces have mostly stopped talking about mood. Conditioned benefit plans still make adherence a workplace variable where courts allow. In Ninth Circuit states HR departments have dropped adherence-feed differentials, and in Eighth Circuit states they keep them. Sales staff no longer time holidays to quarter-end as routine. Casino and sportsbook operators cite the gambling-disorder label in guidance.
interior_life.effect_on_art_and_play: 'Off-dose' billing has faded, and holiday-weekend passes are a novelty act. Comedy about the grey reads as 2031 material. The live genre is appetite: full-plate streams, 'whole table' supper theatre, and novels about the one unmedicated sibling. Gambling handle growth stays below pre-incretin trend.
interior_life.effect_on_intimacy: Sex therapists see reward blunting as one cause among many and step doses down rather than prescribe holidays. Holidays around conception remain standard advice. The intimacy question has moved from 'are you flat?' to 'are you on?', and the honest answer has become a dating variable.
interior_life.effect_on_politics: The ad bar passed with left-populist and religious-right votes, and pro-access populists called it nanny-statism. Gray-market enforcement divides the pro-access bloc: crack down on counterfeits, but don't touch the $38 pen from Juárez. Candidates are still asked if they are on, and now also whether they are 'clean'.

state.regulatory_posture: Pro-access on price and approvals (amycretin, Stratara, gambling disorder), but turning restrictive at the edges. In Mar 2034 the FDA restricted initiation in ages 6–11 to specialists. Congress barred broadcast and social-media DTC for incretin behavioural claims and limited telehealth initiation of behavioural indications to synchronous visits with 90-day fills. Eleven states require a specialist and parental consent for under-18 initiation. PhRMA's First Amendment challenge to the ad bar is pending.
state.subsidy_or_mandate: No mandate to take the drug. Subsidies: the Medicare Bridge ($195/$50, conditional, through 2035), the HRSA programme ($4.4B FY2034, with an annual weigh-in), the DoD Metabolic Readiness Program, the ACA cessation mandate, and SSA II ceiling prices.
state.conditioning_or_surveillance: Ten Medicaid adherence waivers. Bridge continuation tied to response, PDC, DEXA and a function test. Employer adherence-feed differentials are legal in some circuits and barred in others. PBM data are known to be degraded by skip-but-fill, and gray use is invisible to every payer feed. FDA's lot-verification app logs scans, which privacy groups have flagged.
state.workforce_or_military: Metabolic Readiness Program ~190k active duty. Body-composition separations are down ~35% on the pre-programme level. Religious-accommodation requests number ~3,400. The Army added a DEXA screen for members on drug for more than 2 years after stress-fracture reports at basic training. Police and fire contracts persist. FAA special issuance is unchanged.
state.geopolitics_of_supply: Incretins remain Section 232 critical medicines. SSA II extends Lilly's tariff exemption and DPA financing for ceiling prices. India's WTO consultation became a panel request in 2033, and India now publicly declines to police exports. Trans-shipment through the UAE and Singapore and Mexican land-border purchases undercut CBP mail seizures. Novo pays duty and defends its US position through the device-patent injunction.

events.event: FDA approves low-dose orforglipron as an adjunct for gambling disorder and adds a labelled claim for reducing intrusive food and craving thoughts. Lilly launches a 'quiet mind' campaign. The same week, FDA's pooled class analysis moves anhedonia to the 'uncommon' adverse-reaction category at maintenance doses

CDC issues a Health Alert on counterfeit semaglutide pens filled with insulin glargine and on Burkholderia-contaminated gray vials, linked to ~1,300 emergency visits and 32 deaths over 14 months, as gray-market use passes an estimated 14 million Americans

The Federal Circuit upholds a preliminary injunction on Novo's pen-injector patent, freezing generic semaglutide launches that had been scheduled under settlements. Days later Lilly and Novo sign the second Strategic Supply Agreement, cutting TrumpRx prices to $199 for semaglutide, $249 for tirzepatide and $349 for retatrutide

Congress renews the Medicare GLP-1 Bridge through 2035 at $195 a month with a $50 copay, keeps the 5%, adherence and DEXA conditions, adds a chair-stand test, and attaches an annual weigh-in to HRSA's free-drug programme

After the final adolescent bone-accrual study, FDA restricts incretin initiation in children 6–11 to pediatric specialists with baseline DEXA. In the same month Congress bars broadcast and social-media advertising of incretin behavioural claims and limits telehealth starts. PhRMA sues

FDA approves Lilly's bimagrumab-tirzepatide combination Stratara for weight reduction with lean-mass preservation in adults 60 and over, at $599 direct on allocation. Medicare covers it only for users meeting sarcopenia criteria, and Lilly's campaign promises to 'keep the you'

open_tensions: Stratara is sold as the end of skinny-frail on DXA lean-mass data, with no falls or fracture outcome. Medicare pays for it, the incretin and the antiresorptive at once in 75+, and denosumab-rebound fractures are surfacing among people whose combined authorisation ends at a missed condition.

The US generic semaglutide injunction goes to trial in 2035, the year the Bridge and SSA II expire. Meanwhile ~15.6M Americans buy $25–90 gray pens that no payer feed sees, and the counterfeit death count makes enforcement politically necessary and unpopular at once.

The Eighth and Ninth Circuits disagree on whether PBM adherence feeds can set premiums, and the feeds are known to be degraded by skip-but-fill. A Supreme Court petition is filed while ten Medicaid waivers rely on the same data.

The ad bar on behavioural claims, PhRMA's First Amendment suit and the aesthetic inversion pull on the same demand from different sides. Lilly is selling a quiet mind, and appetite has become a status good, at the same moment the label calls flatness an uncommon side effect.
still_true: Wegovy's list price remains $1,349 a month, and almost nobody pays it.
No FDA-approved generic semaglutide or tirzepatide is sold in the US.

Indiana's and Arkansas's 1115 waivers still require ≥80% proportion-of-days-covered and quarterly verified weigh-ins with a 12-month lockout after two misses, and the disability-rights challenge is still unresolved.
The suicidal-ideation warning removed from Wegovy, Zepbound and Saxenda labels in January 2026 has not returned.
The ACA preventive mandate still requires plans to cover semaglutide for smoking cessation in two 90-day courses a year.

prose.headline: Thin Is Cheap Now: The $38 Border Pen, the $599 Muscle Shot, and Why a Full Plate Became the New Status Symbol
prose.world_in_600_words:
By the end of 2034 just over a third of American adults are on an incretin drug, about ninety-four million people. Close to one in six of them gets it from no pharmacy a payer can see. The official price kept falling the way Washington wanted. In November 2033 the second Strategic Supply Agreement set semaglutide at $199 a month on the federal portal, tirzepatide at $249 and retatrutide at $349. That same month a federal appeals court held up generic semaglutide over a patent on the pen itself. The settlements had promised Americans the generic in 2033. Instead they live next to a world where the same molecule costs six dollars in Delhi and thirty-eight across the bridge in Juárez.

That gap filled the gray market. People cut off by missed conditions, priced out or simply impatient buy pens through social-commerce storefronts, through parcels routed via Dubai and through border pharmacies. In August 2033 the CDC traced counterfeit pens filled with insulin and vials contaminated with bacteria to thirty-two deaths and more than a thousand emergency visits. Pharmacies now scan lot numbers into a federal app. Customs seizures doubled, and so did the trade.

Public coverage is still conditional. Congress renewed the Medicare Bridge through 2035 at $195 a month, kept the requirements for five percent weight loss, adherence and an annual bone scan, and added a test of standing up from a chair. Ten states now run adherence waivers in Medicaid. The free liraglutide at community health centres used to ask only that patients collect their refills. It now asks for one weigh-in a year, the price of getting the programme renewed. Employers attach conditions where courts let them. The Eighth Circuit says pharmacy adherence data may set premiums and the Ninth Circuit says they may not, so a petition heads for the Supreme Court.

The bone problem is no longer new. It has become routine. The modelled excess of hip fractures among older users is about twenty-one thousand a year, and doctors prescribe a bone drug alongside the incretin as standard practice. There is a new failure at the seam. When coverage ends at a missed weigh-in, the bone drug often ends with it, and some patients, with nothing tapering them off it, crack vertebrae within a year. In May 2034 the FDA approved Lilly's Stratara, tirzepatide paired with a muscle-sparing antibody, at $599 a month and on allocation. Its trials measured muscle kept on a scan, not falls prevented. The advertisements say 'keep the you.'

The flatness people called 'the grey' has shrunk to a line on the label. A pooled FDA analysis found it in about three percent of users at maintenance doses, against two percent on placebo, and it is now listed as uncommon. Doctors lower the dose and move on. Meanwhile Lilly won approval for its low-dose pill for gambling disorder and for the 'noise' of food cravings, and it advertised a quiet mind until Congress barred broadcast and social-media ads for behavioural claims in March 2034. The same month the FDA limited new prescriptions for children aged six to eleven to specialists, after final data showed that bone gains in adolescence had lagged.

The culture has turned. A thin body is cheap and reads as medicated. In Brooklyn and Silver Lake, women in their late twenties and thirties post 'clean' blood panels on their dating profiles, and in Austin a steakhouse table where everyone finishes is a kind of display. Being unmedicated has become the scarce thing, and so has appetite itself. Packaged food and spirits keep shrinking, fine dining has had its first good years in a decade, and gyms advertise hours on an 'unmedicated floor.' Seen from outside, the country is lean and calm. Inside, it is sorting itself by who pays for their thinness and who visibly does not need it.
prose.a_day_in_the_life:
Denise Ortega parks at the Stanton Street bridge at 6:40, before her shift, with the cooler bag folded in her purse. Her plan at the dental group dropped her in March after two missed coaching calls. The letter called it non-enrolment.

The Farmacia del Puente counter in Juárez smells of floor cleaner. Three boxes of semaglutide, Indian-made, 2.4 mg pens: 2,100 pesos. The clerk turns each box so she can scan it with the federal lot app, which works on Mexican lots now. Green, green, green. She remembers the insulin pens from last summer, the woman in Las Cruces.

Coming back, the CBP officer looks at the cooler. "Personal?"

"Ninety days."

He waves her through.

At work she scales a man who tells her, unprompted, that he's clean, no pen, eats whatever he wants. He says it the way men used to mention their trucks.

At lunch the other hygienists split tacos. Denise eats half and wraps the rest for her daughter Marisol, fifteen, who has started calling food she leaves on her plate 'pen scraps.'

At six her sister texts a photo from a steakhouse in Austin: an empty plate, a bone, the caption *finished it*. Forty-one hearts.

At home Denise lays the boxes in the vegetable drawer beside Marisol's yoghurt. She gives the Sunday shot a day early because she has a feeling about Sunday. Marisol watches from the doorway.

"Do you even like dinner anymore?"

"I like it fine."

She means it, mostly. She clears the table, saves the tacos, and sets an alarm for the weigh-in she no longer has to go to.
